category_title: Students with academic anxiety who use physical gestures to communicate emerging conceptual understanding
minimal_context: Luke is working on a math problem involving negative exponents with his tutor and a peer, trying to get rid of a negative exponent in the denominator.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's look at this negative exponent problem. Try to get rid of the negative exponent in the denominator.

STUDENT: I worked on this one by myself, but I can't figure out how to solve it.

TUTOR: If you want to get rid of the negative exponent in the denominator and make it one number, you have to multiply by the reciprocal. Do you remember what that is?

STUDENT: When you switch right?

TUTOR: Can you explain what you mean by that?

STUDENT: Uh…The same thing, but twist, right? (He responds in an unsure, questioning way, twisting his hand back and forth in a circular motion with his palm facing toward the tutor, looking self-conscious about answering in front of his peer.)

options.A: Agree with the student that he is having a rough time with the math problem, acknowledging his difficulty during the current tutoring session.
options.B: Break the negative exponent problem into small chunks, dividing the material into smaller segments during the current tutoring session as he works on it.
options.C: Observe the student's gesture as a valuable assessment tool and utilize it to guide him through the steps necessary for solving the problem.
options.D: Produce authoritativeness by speaking in short sentences, like headlines in a newspaper; talk briefly and concisely, mentioning only the main details of the problem.
